target: Original Thaumcraft 1.7.10-4.2.3.5 + Baubles 1.7.10-1.0.1.10 on Forge 1.20.1 / Java 17

legacyRuntime.depLoaderNote: The bundled CodeChicken DepLoader coremod scans dependancies.info and would download Baubles from the now-dead dl.dropboxusercontent.com host. Supplying the unmodified Baubles jar in mods/1.7.10 satisfies the check so no download is attempted.

fixes: LegacyContent no longer probes metadata a block does not declare; Thaumcraft blocks such as blockCosmeticOpaque index their icon array by metadata and threw ArrayIndexOutOfBounds for undeclared values, which previously aborted the whole content freeze.
Item icon/name/color lookups now fall back to the item's base unlocalized name instead of failing the freeze.

LegacyContent.Block now records the metadata that actually carry a TileEntity; blockCosmeticSolid and blockHole report hasTileEntity but create no tile for metadata 0, so tile creation is only forced where the old block really supplies one.
LegacyTiles.create returns null for technical blocks that expose no tile instead of throwing, and block drops only read inventories when an old tile exists.
The content smoke probe only requires mapped drops for blocks whose original drop methods actually return an item.

Block items now resolve their icon from the linked block's getIcon(side, metadata); ItemBlock.getIconFromDamage ignores metadata and previously made every variant share the metadata-0 texture (for example all custom ores showed cinnabar).

Block inventory models are chosen from the original render type: cube-like blocks (ores, logs, fluids, devices) render as cubes with their per-face textures, while crosses, crops, doors, fibres and candles stay flat sprites.
The content smoke world deadline was raised to ten minutes and failures are written to the smoke report so the acceptance script can detect them reliably.

Static legacy block models are captured by executing the real old ISimpleBlockRenderingHandler (RenderingRegistry.renderInventoryBlock) inside a LegacyWorldGraphics capture, then replayed through a modern custom item renderer.

Icon identity is recovered without running the old texture stitcher: IIcon proxies assign each texture a synthetic atlas cell, so a captured quad's UV range identifies its source icon, whose local UVs are remapped onto the modern block atlas sprite.
Fixed texture sampling: TextureAtlasSprite.getU/getV expect a 0..16 icon coordinate, not 0..1; using 0..1 sampled a single pixel column (uniform gray).

Custom item models use builtin/entity registered through Item.initializeClient (Forge 47.4.28 has no RegisterClientExtensionsEvent), and the captured geometry is shifted by +0.5 because BlockRenderer.drawFaces centers it with glTranslatef(-0.5).

Legacy display lists are now an ordered event stream of command and local-space geometry entries: GL_COMPILE records without touching the outer matrix, glCallList replays in order with recursive expansion, and glDrawArrays rejects nesting inside glBegin/glEnd.

The old Forge IItemRenderer path is captured by executing MinecraftForgeClient.getItemRenderer(INVENTORY) with the catalog stack's NBT, which is what makes wands (whose appearance depends on rod/cap NBT) render; the fake client now also provides Minecraft.timer and RenderManager.textureManager that these renderers read.

A host item with no legacy representation (for example modern oak_wood) now leaves its mirrored slot empty instead of throwing, so one unknown item can no longer abort legacy container initialization.
The fake client player now initializes EntityLivingBase.activePotionsMap, which old wand tooltips (WandManager.getTotalVisDiscount) read and previously crashed on.
remaining: Modern registration covers blocks/items and simple or tile-backed placement; Thaumcraft's wands, alchemy, vis network, research and custom rendering are not functional yet.
Blocks needing special render types (renderType != 0) are declared but not placeable through the generic bridge.
Original GUIs, Tessellator/display-list world rendering, entities and old network packets remain unsupported as in the AcademyCraft phase.
